# Allegro.pl Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/allegro-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/allegro-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects product data from Allegro.pl, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Allegro.pl in 2026 (Without Getting Blocked)](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-allegro)
- **Code:** [`allegro.py`](allegro.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Product](results/product.json) · [Search](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Allegro product pages for product listing data
- Allegro product search

## Functions

- `scrape_search(query, max_pages=3, scrape_all_pages=False)` → `List[Dict]`: Scrape Allegro search pages for product listings
- `scrape_product(urls)` → `Dict`: scrape a single Allegro product

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import allegro


async def main():
    search = await allegro.scrape_search("Cooler CPU")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/product.json`](results/product.json): `title`, `price`, `images`, `shipping_info`, `rating`, `specifications`, `seller`, `reviews`, `allegro_smart_badge`
- [`results/search.json`](results/search.json): `products`, `scraped_pages`, `products_count`, `total_pages`, `total_count`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`allegro.py`](allegro.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser
- `retry` = `True`: retry a failed request

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/allegro-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_product_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
